[From REDCap project to quality-checked report.]{.accent} This kit pulls records from REDCap with REDCapR, uses the project's own data dictionary to drive cleaning and labelling, runs six data quality checks, and renders a status report. It is demonstrated on a fictional pregnancy cohort with synthetic data. ::: {.project-note} It is demonstrated on the **Coastal Beginnings Study**, a fictional pregnancy cohort. **All data are simulated. No real people are represented.** ::: ## What it does 1. **Defines a realistic REDCap project.** A longitudinal data dictionary with three events, required fields, range validation, branching logic, calculated fields (BMI, gestational age, a preterm flag), cross-event references, and identifier flags on dates. 2. **Pulls the data** live from the REDCap API with [REDCapR](https://ouhscbbmc.github.io/REDCapR/), or from a local REDCap-format export when no credentials are set. 3. **Cleans it using the data dictionary.** Field types and labels come from the dictionary, not hard-coded rules, so the same code adapts to other projects. 4. **Runs six quality checks** and writes a list of issues a study coordinator can work through. 5. **Renders a Quarto report** with recruitment, follow-up, data quality, baseline characteristics, and outcome graphics. ## The sample report ::: {.report-card} ![](images/report-preview.png){fig-alt="Preview of the Coastal Beginnings report"} ::: {} ### Coastal Beginnings Study A data status and quality report, generated automatically from the REDCap project. It is a single self-contained file, so a study coordinator can email it or open it offline. [Read the sample report](report/index.html){.btn .btn-accent} ::: ::: ## What's here - **[How it works](how-it-works.qmd):** the pipeline, the six quality checks, and how to use it with a real REDCap project. - **[Sample report](report/index.html):** the report the kit produces for the fictional Coastal Beginnings Study. - **[About the data](about.qmd):** where the data come from, the licences, and who made this.
